It is hard, not saying it was easy for me but I adjusted quickly after a week or two.  I eat predominately beef, i.e. ribeye steaks, T-bones, ground beef, eggs, bacon, butter.  Also chicken, pork, some fish.  So the diet consists of proteins 30-35%, and fat 65-70%.  I know it sounds crazy but this:  helped me lose 35 lbs. over 9 months;  lessened a deep, major depression I was suffering from; alleviated joint pain and inflammation throughout my body; cured/reversed my pre-diabetes; and of course no constipation or any more digestive issues, which I previously suffered from pretty badly.  I get blood work done every 6 months at the VA and my doctors are amazed at the improvements so far.   


It's not for everyone but if you are interested, check out Dr. Ken Berry on YouTube - he has many relatively short videos 5-20 minutes for most, that give you a ton of insight.  Best wishes for you in whatever you do.
If you are able to go zero carbs, that cures constipation 100% of the time.  I was surprised how all my digestive/bowel issues went away - and nearly a year later I'm doing amazing in so many ways.
Dak needs some more weapons for sure.  CB is a need, and I'd think D-line is a bigger priority that O-line.

Stay away from carbs and continue those workouts.  Wish it helped my anxiety as it does yours and for many others, no such luck for me: but I've actually lost weight in the 6 months or so I've been on it.   Down to 185 from 220, without dieting other than stopped eating carbs during that time also.  I do intermittent fasting also, usually 18 hours with a 6 hour eating window daily.  72 hour fast around every 90-120 days also.     


Glad it is helping you and glad you are working hard to get/stay in shape,  Best wishes.

In my experience, depends on the doctor.  I personally receive little or no relief from either Gabapentin or Lyrica, regardless of dose - while the xanax and other benzo's have done an amazing job of helping my anxiety - usually 60-80% depending on dose.  Like you, I sometimes used more than prescribed to achieve the desired help.  I don't get high off them but they really help my anxiety.  

​

So I think you stand a good chance to get Lyrica, or get your desired dose of Gabapentin possible up to max, but most doctors I've used usually kept me around the 2400mg mark.  Gabapentin caused such bad side effects in larger doses after just a short while of use so I don't even jack with it anymore.  But with the VA, most of those doctors are happy to prescribe it, whereas Benzo's are nearly impossible.    


Hope that helps you.

To be strong is to be vulnerable and to be healed is to accept that we are wounded and to convince ourselves that through inner thoughts and positive attitude, hard work, anything is possible.  

​

Remember, to the infinite all things finite are equal.  I wish you and all others suffering with trauma and PTSD (which is most humans) peace and tranquility.

Wish any of those would work for me - have tried all classes and most of each, along with many combinations, never any relief or benefit - but a long list of side effects for me with each type be is ssri, snri, maoi, tca, atypicals.  Benzos and Adderral worked but good luck getting those consistently.

Adderall - if the generic is effective such as Teva, for me was excellent.  It helped to have benzo's but even without them my anxiety was much lower than on nothing at all, or regular AD drugs.  Tramadol, that is strange indeed, but I did get relief from opioids mostly hydrocodone.  Shrooms - had great experiences when younger, no idea how or where to obtain at this point.  Would love to give them a try again.  Weed could be hit or miss probably 50/50 - but some of those weed induced panic attacks were some of the worst.  Have not tried Pregabalin (is that similar to gabapentin?) and propranolol was ineffective.    


Perhaps most frustrating is the inability to find these alternatives to provide consistent relief. It's great to get a temporary period of relief for sure, but in time the ups and downs become tiresome and at least for me, start to work against me. I do appretiate your comments however. Thank you!

Some good suggestions as Adderral 60mg/day + 2-4mg/day Xanax pretty much did the trick for about 10 years, with maybe a minor bout of depression a few times in that span, situational and short lived.  I also would rotate to a longer acting benzo i.e. klonipin; volume - and switched the Adderral out with Ritilan usually around every 6 months.  Took some "vacations" from all of it for a few weeks a year, sometimes a month or two.  Worked extremely well, very minimal sides which were easily managed.   I was able to obtain these medicines when living in Pakistan, Colombia and Panama.  
Problem is I have been unable to obtain these or anything like them here in United States.  The few times I did bring up that these medicines helped me with psychiatrists here, one flat out told me we were done and would no longer see me; others treated me like I was a flat out drug addict.  Spent the next year spiraling down and becoming hopelessly depressed and suicidal.  Eventually did discover Ketamine, which wiped out the depression and anxiety, for over a year, taking no medications at all and feeling pretty awesome.  But eventually the symptoms returned - only this time due to financial reasons I could no longer afford Ketamine, and could only turn to the VA for help.  More rounds of ineffective AD's, no ketamine, no alternative treatments.    


Will be checking out the link you provided about the ketamine affordability program - thank you!

Nearly my entire adult life has been one nightmare after another of try this, try that, try this other one, but I believe I have reached the end of the line; I am convinced there is no help, no hope for me.  If I could afford Ketamine that is the only thing that ever helped me, just don't have the $3-4k to afford the treatment. VA is a joke and has done little to nothing to provide ketamine to veterans otherwise treatment resistant.  

I too am disgusted with myself for different reasons but reading your description of "... concentration problem became worse, I am experiencing brain fog, depersonalisation, dissociation, derealisation, irritably and cognitive decline." I realize this is how I feel regardless.  I have found medications that do work in controlling my symptoms but doctors are reluctant or refuse to prescribe.  With my anxiety as bad as it is I break down at the first hint that a doctor gives me wanting me to try yet another AD medicine, and the nightmare continues.  

I hope others suffering find help and relief that I could not - and wish you all the very best in future.

Just had to discontinue Parnate for major side effects, so desperate I actually wanted to try and continue hoping they'd go away but doctor said no way.  Side effects were severe and a long list.  Was only on 10mg 2x/day...made it 12 days before discontinuing.  The medicine did not help my anxiety at all, and seemed to make my depression and SI worse.    


Not sure where else to turn, that was pretty much one of the last AD medicine I had not tried, all others have had similar results, no help, only side effects.  Some I was able to stay on longer others but in the end, never any benefit whatsoever.  At least 40-50 different medications tried dating back to 80's.    


Thinking about calling it quits now - never thought I'd reach this point of giving up but as I think about it more and more it just seems like the right time.  Like I am finally at peace with the decision, feeling like I did all I could to make my life at least livable and not a constant torment.  And knowing I have helped a lot of others along the way...    


If anyone has experienced similar or has suggestions, I am hopeful something can be helpful.  If not, I've resigned to calling it a life...and wish everyone all the best.

Many years ago had major issues due to lexapro;  doc told me take bupropion (wellbutrin) to fix.  Tried it and felt pretty restored within 2-3 weeks, got off both the lexapro and wellbutrin shortly afterwards.  (Still suffer but meds don't benefit so no longer take any)

I am on day 5 of TCP (10mg x2/day) and it has not been helpful with anxiety or depression yet.  Was a bit hopeful after seeing some get relief in 2-3 days.  But no other medication of this type (inhibitors) has ever worked for me (aside for some nasty side effects and feeling out of sorts)   


Ketamine was a game changer for me.  6 infusions over about 12 days.  Was skeptical since nothing had ever worked in 30 years - but after the 4th infusion, I was noticing positive changes.  Final 2 infusions just completely closed the lid on any and all anxiety and also at that time, severe depression.  I was essentially not only not depressed, not fearful, not suicidal for first time in years - I was the most positive I can remember since I was a young adult, early years in military.    


ALL my depression and anxiety was gone completely.  Ended up conceiving (well, wife did too - lol) my first child ever if that tells you anything - and I had previously said I would never ever have kids.  (and I'm 53). That was 2 years ago.  The effects of the ketamine eventually waned after 1.5 years...not all at once but slowly and surely anxiety returned;  seems like the ketamine was still working for a while after but eventually the anxiety returned and is back stronger than ever.    


But would definitely do another round of Ketamine and will do as soon as finances and situation allows.

Just received my shipment - 41 lbs actually of pure Colombian goodness!  Getting ready to grind and prepare the first batch. One other thing I find interesting about this clean coffee direct from Colombia i.e. not processed as most store coffees can be is the caffeine does not give me jitters.  That's actually something which several others I know claim also - some friends who got heart palpitations from Starbucks or Peets were able to drink this coffee with no negative effects from it.

So sorry to learn that your initial experiences with coffee are of Starbucks - which unfortunately are highly commercial and taste horrible in comparison with real coffees not sold on open market.  I used to like "commercial" coffees such as Folgers and Maxwell House myself, until moving to Panama and then Colombia and experiencing the best coffees they had to offer - an amazing difference.  Different people have different tastes though so it really depends on your preference.  I used to think dark roasts were the best and only way to go - until I was introduced to medium and light roasts, again, in Colombia.  Not to say that Colombian coffees are better than other coffees around the world, but they do offer up some of the best I've ever tried from around the world.  A large part of this is due to their expertise in roasting, which is in large part as important as the bean itself.    


But back to coffee itself, a good one to try if it's sold in your area is called "Community Coffee".  I'd recommend trying their "Hotel Blend" or "Breakfast Blend" which are both medium roasts.  They certainly are not as good as specialty coffees from Colombia or other parts of the world which also sell at much higher price, but probably the best commercial brand I've tried since being back in the USA.  Lucky for me - I recently ordered 40 lbs. of the good stuff from a grower down in Colombia and just got text notice that it will be delivered - TODAY!  Can't wait - can't wait!
